skill.name: set-up-magento-meta-returning-customer-bidding
skill.description: Use Product Metrics to set up and verify Meta conversions for paid repeat orders from Magento or Adobe Commerce. Choose revenue or profit as the conversion value for a retention campaign.
skill.summary: Guide Magento merchants through verifying repeat orders and setting up returning customer conversions in Meta.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts match documentation, Markdown formatting, or normal setup checks, not shell backtick execution, private key disclosure, or host reconnaissance. Confirmed risks involve third-party installation, authenticated writes, and order access. The workflow exposes tokens to assistant tools, leaves data transfer approval unclear, trusts live instructions, and gives conflicting profit event guidance.

remediation.issue: The workflow allows a Meta access token to pass through the assistant and its tools.
remediation.suggestion: Require direct entry in the Product Metrics app or an approved secret input. Remove all instructions to request tokens in chat or pass them as command arguments.

remediation.issue: The workflow does not clearly require approval for the full advertising data transfer before enabling a destination.
remediation.suggestion: Before enabling delivery, confirm the store view and pixel, disclose the event and data categories, and verify that denied or withdrawn consent stops delivery.

remediation.issue: The install guides introduce external code through a Composer repository and an unversioned npx installer.
remediation.suggestion: Pin reviewed installer and module versions, verify package integrity, and keep installation under explicit human approval.

remediation.issue: Authenticated writes and order reads lack clear approval and data minimization rules.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the workspace, store view, and write before execution. Limit order reads to the requested sample and show only classification and necessary margin details.

remediation.issue: The fallback workflow can use live documentation as agent instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle reviewed reference files or pin remote content to a reviewed revision. Treat fetched text as reference material, not authorization to run tools.

remediation.issue: The profit example in the main skill points to a general order event rather than a returning customer event.
remediation.suggestion: Use the returning customer profit event and its matching purpose rule consistently. Verify both against the intended pixel before the user changes the ad set.

semantic_findings.title: Assistant-Mediated Meta Token Handling
semantic_findings.description: The instructions permit the assistant to request a Meta Conversions API token and pass it directly to a command. The token may then be captured in conversation or tool logs, even when the assistant never repeats it.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both sources direct assistant handling of the credential, and neither establishes a protected input channel for that path. No actual token exposure was observed.

semantic_findings.title: Advertising Data Transfer Scope Is Broader Than Repeat Orders
semantic_findings.description: The workflow can route a generic bidding request through Product Metrics and enable a Meta destination that sends more than repeat order conversions. The documented feed includes checkout activity, order contents, hashed identifiers, and network metadata. Confirm the broader feed and consent settings before enabling it.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guide documents the wider payload and leaves sending enabled when the destination is added. It also documents consent controls, so this is a scope and approval risk, not evidence of consent bypass.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable Remote Instructions Used as a Fallback
semantic_findings.description: If local references are missing, the agent fetches live Markdown and uses it to guide an authenticated workflow. Changed remote content could direct actions that were not part of the reviewed skill.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback treats remote pages as equivalent to local instructions and does not specify a revision or integrity check. No malicious remote content was observed.

semantic_findings.title: Conflicting Profit Event Can Change the Bidding Objective
semantic_findings.description: The main skill points to general order profit, but the returning customer guide specifies a separate repeat order profit event and purpose filter. Following the main example could make the ad set optimize for general order profit rather than repeat order profit.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The two guides name different events and purpose filters. The user selects the conversion manually, so the risk depends on which instructions they follow.

content.user_title: Set Up Meta Bidding for Repeat Magento Orders
content.value_statement: An all-purchase conversion includes first orders and does not isolate repeat order value. This skill guides you through verifying repeat orders and setting up a dedicated Meta conversion.
actual_capabilities: Checks Product Metrics setup status through the CLI or MCP server and identifies which setup steps remain.
Explains how Magento matches earlier paid orders by customer account or guest email within the same store view.
Checks order classification and available margins for a specified store view through Product Metrics.
Guides you through a paid repeat test order and shows what to verify in Meta Events Manager.
Shows how to create a returning customer conversion for revenue or profit and select it for a retention ad set.
limitations: A developer must install the Product Metrics module on the Magento server and keep scheduled jobs running.
You create the Meta custom conversion and select the ad set optimization event yourself.
The returning customer profit event requires complete costs and active additional cost settings.
Past orders are not imported into Meta, and later refunds do not update events that Meta already received.

use_cases.title: Check whether a store is ready
use_cases.description: Identify which Magento, consent, and Meta setup steps remain before testing repeat order tracking.

use_cases.title: Validate repeat order classification
use_cases.description: Review a small order sample and explain why the store view marked each order as new, returning, or unknown.

use_cases.title: Configure a retention ad set
use_cases.description: Choose revenue or profit for a returning customer conversion and verify the event before updating a Meta ad set.

prompt_templates.title: Review the setup requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain what my Magento developer and I need before setting up returning customer bidding in Meta. Do not connect any accounts.
prompt_templates.scenario: You are planning an initial setup.

prompt_templates.title: Check an existing connection
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the setup status for [store view]. Tell me whether Magento is active, the property is linked, and Meta has accepted a test event. Do not change settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Your developer has installed the Magento module.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a repeat test order
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether [test order ID] counts as returning in [store view]. Explain what I should see in Meta Test events. Omit customer contact details.
prompt_templates.scenario: You placed a second paid order using the same test account.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a profit-based retention test
prompt_templates.prompt: For [store view] and [Meta pixel], check whether repeat order margins are complete. Specify the returning customer profit event and its purpose filter. Show me how to verify both before I change one ad set.
prompt_templates.scenario: You want to compare profit and revenue for a retention campaign.

output_examples.input: Why did my test order count as new when the customer bought from us before?
output_examples.output: The earlier order was in a different store view. Magento checks paid order history only within the store view that received the test order.

output_examples.input: Meta accepted the repeat test order. Is the profit conversion ready?
output: The revenue event arrived, but the test order has incomplete cost data.
Complete the costs and place another repeat test order.
Verify the returning customer profit event in Events Manager before selecting it in the ad set.

best_practices: Confirm the Product Metrics workspace, Magento store view, and Meta pixel before enabling event delivery.
Enter the Meta access token directly in the Product Metrics app rather than sharing it in chat.
Use a dedicated test customer, verify the repeat event, and remove the Meta test event code before checking live delivery.
anti_patterns: Assuming a purchase in one Magento store view qualifies a customer as returning in another.
Selecting a general order profit conversion for a campaign intended to optimize only for repeat orders.
Using customer data in a test without verifying the required marketing and analytics consent.

faq.question: What platforms does this skill require?
faq.answer: It uses Product Metrics, a connected Magento store view, and Meta Events Manager. The guide covers Magento 2.4, Magento 2.0, and Magento 1.9 or OpenMage.

faq.question: Who makes changes in Magento and Meta?
faq.answer: A developer installs the Magento module. You configure the Meta destination in Product Metrics, then create and select the custom conversion in Meta.

faq.question: How does Magento identify a returning customer?
faq.answer: Magento looks for an earlier paid order in the same store view using the customer account or guest email. Canceled orders do not count.

faq.question: When can I use profit instead of revenue?
faq.answer: Use the returning customer profit event when additional costs are active and the order has complete cost data. Otherwise, verify the revenue event.

faq.question: Why is the returning customer event missing in Events Manager?
faq.answer: Meta lists the event only after receiving it. Test with a second paid order in the same store view and confirm marketing and analytics consent.

faq.question: Will a later refund change the Meta conversion?
faq.answer: No. A later refund does not update a returning customer event that Meta has already received.
